{{Short description|Algorithm for determining whether a number is prime}}
In [[computational number theory]], the '''Adleman–Pomerance–Rumely primality test''' is an [[algorithm]] for determining whether a number is [[prime number|prime]]. Unlike other, more efficient algorithms for this purpose, it avoids the use of random numbers, so it is a [[deterministic algorithm|deterministic]] [[primality test]]. It is named after its discoverers, [[Leonard Adleman]], [[Carl Pomerance]], and [[Robert Rumely]]. The test involves arithmetic in [[cyclotomic field]]s.

It was later improved by [[Henri Cohen (number theorist)|Henri Cohen]] and [[Hendrik Willem Lenstra]], commonly referred to as '''APR-CL'''. It can test primality of an integer ''n'' in time:

: <math>(\log n)^{O(\log\,\log\,\log n)}.</math>

== Software implementations ==
* [[UBASIC]] provides an implementation under the name APRT-CLE (APR Test CL extended)
*A [http://www.alpertron.com.ar/ECM.HTM factoring applet] that uses APR-CL on certain conditions (source code included)
*[https://web.archive.org/web/20190929045643/http://pari.math.u-bordeaux.fr/ Pari/GP] uses APR-CL conditionally in its implementation of isprime().
*[https://sourceforge.net/projects/mpzaprcl/ mpz_aprcl] is an open source implementation using C and GMP.
*[http://jpenne.free.fr/index2.html Jean Penné's LLR] uses APR-CL on certain types of prime tests as a fallback option.
